title: Functions Associated with Projects
coreMove: Start with the project functions that must be performed, then assign titles, authority, and records so coordination, communication, decisions, facilitation, and learning actually happen.

exampleSpecs.audience: project manager starting a mixed delivery effort
exampleSpecs.stakes: a clean role slide may hide uncovered decision support
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Bernard notices his own title-first error before the sponsor joins

exampleSpecs.stakes: a steering call may reopen settled reasoning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Cassidy writes the action into the decision log instead of relying on hallway memory

exampleSpecs.domain: adaptive release blocked by vendor delay
exampleSpecs.audience: team lead comparing title-first and function-first responses
exampleSpecs.stakes: the same delay can become confusion or coordinated action
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Yvon waits on the project manager title while Margot distributes functions

exampleSpecs.audience: workstream lead who confuses status with decision support
exampleSpecs.stakes: governance may receive data without options or consequences
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Folake reframes Serge's packet from raw status to decision support

exampleSpecs.audience: learner new to PMBOK role-neutral language
exampleSpecs.stakes: confusing the project manager title with every project function
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Agathe's confusion about the project manager role becomes the lesson

exampleSpecs.audience: delivery lead trying to prevent repeated confusion
exampleSpecs.stakes: lessons may arrive after the team has already repeated the error
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Folake shows the same learning process before and after records are used during delivery
